text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy on Monday blamed weak metal markets for a 92 percent slump in its January-August profit, repeating a warning that full-year earnings will be considerably weaker than 1995.

Reporting profit before extraordinary items and tax slid to 109 million markka ($23.9 million) from 1.32 billion in the year-ago period, Outokumpu said prices fell sharpest in copper, ferrochrome and stainless steel.
"The result for the financial year 1996 will be considerably weaker than in 1995," Outokumpu said in a statement.
"Although the group's financial performance is expected to improve to some extent in late 1996, the result of the last tertial will also be poor," it said.
In 1995, the group reported a 1.48 billion markka profit before extraordinaries and tax on net sales of 16.95 billion.

January-August net sales shrank only slightly to 11.08 billion markka from 11.15 billion, but Outokumpu's operating profit collapsed to 331 million from 1.36 billion and earnings per share to 0.28 markka from 7.54.

Its stock was down one markka at 80.00 in slow early Helsinki trade, with the result at the low end of forecasts. The median of analysts' forecasts had been for a 237 million markka profit in a 110-389 million markka range.

Describing a 304 million markka operating loss at its base metals division over the period as "weaker than expected", Outokumpu blamed low metal prices and inventory losses, plus special charges in the second tertial.
It said the division would remain loss-making in 1996.
Currently very low copper inventories were likely to rise again towards the end of 1996, Outokumpu said.
"Copper was the only Outokumpu-produced base that showed some growth in consumption from 1995, whereas the consumption of nickel and zinc declined," it said.

"Copper inventories are at a very low level at the moment, but increasing supply toward year-end is predicted to result in growth in inventories. Nickel and zinc inventories are still higher than normal," it said.

In stainless steel, where the average German transaction price fell 16 percent from the first to the second tertial, Outokumpu said "market conditions have remained unchanged except for a slight decline in prices".
The outlook for stainless steel markets remain clouded by uncertainty: but demand is expected to grow and prices to rise somewhat by the end of the year, the company said.

Overall economic growth was also expected to speed up in Europe in late 1996, and demand for metals and metal products was expected to strengthen as a result, Outokumpu said. ($ = 4.564 Finnish Markka)
